groups.summary: Fetch keyword time series, compare terms on a shared scale, or calculate changes in interest.

groups.summary: Resolve topic IDs, inspect regional interest, and discover related queries or category demand.

groups.title: Research keyword batches
groups.summary: Normalize keyword batches and submit research jobs for later retrieval.

groups.title: Discover live trends and research candidates
groups.summary: Read current searches and their news context, or collect candidates for local research.

groups.title: Track changes and query saved history
groups.summary: Record observations, inspect changes, and analyze data retained by the server.

groups.title: Query published weekly rankings
groups.summary: Read top and rising terms from Google’s public BigQuery tables; coverage is limited to recorded terms.

entries.summary: Explore keyword growth, related queries, topic IDs, regional interest, and hosted SEO opportunity research.
notes: Community and hosted registrations are separate server surfaces: 16 community tools and 6 hosted tools.

entries.summary: Explore keyword time series, regional interest, and topic suggestions with configurable Taiwan defaults.
notes: Daily and realtime search tools rely on legacy pytrends endpoints; they are registered, but current upstream availability was not tested.

entries.summary: Save country RSS snapshots, compare local history, measure velocity, and export reports.
notes: Google Trends keyword search is not implemented; search_trends skips that source. Historical analyses use saved snapshots, not Google’s historical keyword-interest series.
Select google_trends through sources/source when a tool supports source filtering. Content-writing and other-source tools remain documented separately.

entries.summary: Resolve topic IDs, compare search properties, and discover category or regional demand.
notes: Google Trends Explore supports trendspy or DataForSEO backends; current trending searches always use trendspy. DataForSEO’s own demography/subregion datasets are not Google Trends.
Default locale is German/DE; language and geo are caller parameters where registered.

entries.summary: Compare keyword interest, retrieve related queries, and rank regional interest.
notes: All three Trends tools accept timeframe but do not pass it to the request implementation. The registered default is not an implemented time filter.

entries.summary: Fetch keyword interest or joint comparisons, plus current trending searches.
Compare terms and normalize larger keyword batches with a shared anchor, synchronously or as saved jobs.
notes: Async submission/status require an initialized research_tasks SQLite table; the stdio entrypoint does not initialize it.

entries.summary: Compare live trends across regions, diff fresh observations, and query archived snapshots or keyword interest.
notes: Historical trending lookup covers only locally recorded observations. Enable archive on fresh fetches to build that history.
The keyword-interest and full Trending Now CSV tools require a local Chrome browser; RSS tools do not.

entries.summary: Explore keyword time series, regional interest, related searches, categories, and location codes.
notes: Use the default trendspy backend. The optional official backend is a stub that raises NotImplementedError.
Related-query and related-topic tools are implemented, but their descriptions warn of upstream quota failures.

entries.summary: Select time series, geographic interest, related queries, or related topics through one hosted tool.
notes: The schema was captured from the hosted tools/list endpoint. A HasData API key is required by the connector; hosted execution and validation were not tested.

entries.summary: Read current Google Trends RSS terms and optional related-news metadata, alongside news-search tools.
notes: The only Google Trends tool is get_trending_terms; the other four tools search or summarize news.

entries.summary: Query top terms, rising terms, or recorded weekly scores for one term and country.
notes: Requires a Google Cloud project and application-default credentials. Country values are validated in implementation, not an input-schema enum.
comparar_termo_tool retrieves one term’s recorded history; it does not compare multiple terms. Registrations provide no descriptions, so the English behavior summaries come from SQL source.

entries.summary: Fetch time series, related queries, regional interest, and current country RSS searches.
notes: Requires compatible MCP 1.x. The repository’s unbounded MCP dependency can resolve to incompatible 2.x imports.

entries.summary: Query live interest, regions, and related terms; inspect cached changes, seasonality, and historical trending snapshots.
notes: The server exposes 27 registrations, including generated command mirrors; req inputs on low-level endpoints are JSON-encoded strings.
import always errors. workflow_archive archives zero records, and default sync has no resources. Parent trends/trends_history/workflow tools provide guidance rather than data.
Local-history tools require retained observations; trends_trending_at does not retrieve arbitrary historical dates from Google.

entries.summary: Read country RSS trending searches, traffic lower bounds, and related news through one local tool.
notes: The local server has one tool. The documented hosted scoped gateway also exposes 40 shared tools unrelated to Google Trends; their complete schemas are retained for completeness and excluded from capability grouping.
Hosted gateway registrations were captured through tools/list; shared gateway implementations are not public.
entries.count_label: 1 local tool; hosted gateway also documented

entries.summary: Fetch time series, compare terms, inspect related queries or regional interest, and read current RSS searches.
notes: Advertised JSON Schema and stricter Zod handler validation differ; both are documented without merging them.

entries.summary: Collect US trending candidates and single-keyword research into local runs; MCP returns paths and reads saved summaries.
notes: ask/discover return paths, not raw Google Trends series. Keyword interest and top related queries are saved as raw files; post summaries do not incorporate those measurements.
discover can place Google Trends candidate names in a saved summary readable through read_summary; it is not a keyword comparison or region-interest tool.
Requires reachable Ollama and instantiates other source clients even when Google Trends alone is selected. Experimental Reddit-only prototypes are excluded from the production list.

entries.summary: Request hosted keyword series, point-to-point growth, and current overall or category boards.
notes: Requires a TrendsMCP API key. Local schemas are verified; the hosted MCP endpoint’s schema equivalence is unverified.
Tools multiplex Google Trends with other sources. Provider retrieval and growth calculations are proprietary; geographic breakdowns are not exposed.
